storage: Close must not rewrite the snapshot when the session wrote nothing. Surfaced by v1.1-coi-screen-real-corpus (#594): a read-only consumer rewrites the 1.1 GB snapshot.mmap on every exit (8.3 s / 7.9 GB; JSON 25 s / 17.5 GB). Acceptance: mtime and bytes unchanged after a read-only open/close, changed after one write, both seen red first; WAL truncate stays tied to a snapshot that happened. Spec row in NEXT_STEPS_2026-06-18.md section D

storage: JSON-mode Close must not rewrite snapshot.json when the session wrote nothing. Same defect as v1.4-close-no-rewrite-when-clean (#598) on the other representation: a read-only consumer pays 25 s / 17.5 GB per exit on the 2.0M-node ICIJ store. JSON has no overlay, so the proof differs: WAL empty at open and LSN unchanged since, plus every unlogged mutation path (index definitions, SetEncryption, DeleteAllNodes) accounted for. BulkImportMode has no WAL and must always write. Acceptance: snapshot.json mtime and bytes unchanged after a read-only open/close, changed after one write, both seen red first; WAL truncate stays tied to a snapshot that happened

storage: a WAL append failure must not be reported to the caller as success. Today enqueueWAL (9 sites, node and edge ops), waitWALPending (14 sites) and writeToWAL (6 sites, property and vector index definitions) print to stderr and return nil; the in-memory mutation stays, the WAL entry is missing, and until #602 Close could drop it. Decide and implement one contract: the caller gets an error and the in-memory change is rolled back, or the store refuses further writes until a snapshot lands. Acceptance: with a write fault on the WAL file, no public write method returns nil; a test per path family, each seen red first; replay after a crash never lacks a write the API confirmed. Interface change: propose the contract to the user before code

api,graphql: map storage.ErrWALWriteFailed to a response that stops a client retry. Since v1.4-wal-write-errors-reach-the-caller a single-op write returns ErrWALWriteFailed with the entity applied in memory; the REST and GraphQL handlers surface it as a generic error, and a client that retries creates a second node. Acceptance: the REST status and body and the GraphQL error extension say the write applied and must not be retried, and carry the entity ID; one handler test per surface, each seen red first

storage: a snapshot records the WAL boundary LSN it covers, and replay skips entries at or below it. Today a Close whose snapshot lands but whose WAL truncate fails for any cause (disk error at exit) leaves entries the snapshot already holds, and the next open replays them: a create from before a delete resurrects the deleted entity. Additive field in the JSON snapshot and in the mmap metadata tail (no version bump needed if absent means 0); replay compares entry.LSN to it. Acceptance: with the truncate forced to fail after a successful snapshot, a deleted node stays deleted after reopen, on both formats, seen red first
